report_name: North Korean Hackers Use Public Blockchain for Covert C2 Channel

threat_actors.name: Alluring Pisces
threat_actors.description: A North Korean state-sponsored threat group that uses a public blockchain for command-and-control (C2) communications in sophisticated software supply chain attacks targeting cloud credentials.
threat_actors.goals: To steal cloud credentials (IAM keys, CI/CD tokens) from developer environments and CI/CD pipelines by poisoning open-source packages.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The group poisons open-source software packages on npm, Go, and Packagist to gain initial access to developer environments and CI/CD pipelines.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The malware queries a smart contract on a public blockchain to retrieve the current C2 server address, abusing a legitimate decentralized application-layer service for resilient C2 communications.

attack_patterns.name: Asymmetric Cryptography
attack_patterns.description: The smart contract used for C2 has an update function protected by the attacker's private key, an example of using asymmetric cryptography to control C2 infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The primary goal of the malware is to steal cloud credentials, such as IAM keys and CI/CD tokens, from compromised developer environments and build pipelines.

malware.name: Shai-Hulud
malware.description: A malware family that includes the ChainDrop worm. It is used to infect open-source packages to harvest credentials.

malware.name: ChainDrop
malware.description: A self-propagating worm from the Shai-Hulud family that has infected over 400 npm packages. It uses a `preinstall` hook to activate a credential harvester.

malware.name: PolinRider
malware.description: Malware that hides loaders in repository configuration files like `devcontainer.json` and IDE settings, causing the payload to execute when a developer opens the compromised project.

campaigns.name: ChainDrop
campaigns.description: A campaign by Alluring Pisces using the ChainDrop worm to poison hundreds of npm packages to steal cloud credentials.

campaigns.name: PolinRider
campaigns.description: A campaign by Alluring Pisces that spreads across multiple package ecosystems (npm, Go, Packagist) to steal cloud credentials by hiding loaders in repository and IDE configuration files.

infrastructure.name: Blockchain C2 Channel
infrastructure.description: A C2 mechanism using a smart contract on a public blockchain to store and retrieve the address of the actual C2 server. This makes the C2 resolution highly resilient and resistant to takedowns.

indicators.name: Anomalous Build Environment Egress to Blockchain APIs
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Build Environment Egress to Blockchain APIs
id: 2b1c8d9e-4f5a-4b6c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects processes associated with package managers (npm, go, composer) making outbound network connections to known public blockchain API endpoints. This could indicate a compromised dependency attempting to resolve a blockchain-based C2 channel, as used by Alluring Pisces.
references:
  - https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/cloud-supply-chain-attacks/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1071
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\go.exe'
      - '\composer.phar'
  selection_dest:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - '.infura.io'
      - '.alchemy.com'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer tools or dependencies that interact with blockchain services.
indicators.description: Detects build tools making outbound connections to public blockchain APIs, a technique used by Alluring Pisces for C2 resolution.

indicators.name: Suspicious NPM Preinstall Hook Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious NPM Preinstall Hook Execution
id: 8a7b6c5d-4e3f-4a2b-8c1d-0e9f8a7b6c5d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the execution of a 'preinstall' script by the Node Package Manager (npm). While this can be legitimate, it is a known vector for supply chain attacks, such as the ChainDrop campaign by Alluring Pisces, to execute malicious code upon package installation.
references:
  - https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/cloud-supply-chain-attacks/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\npm.cmd'
    CommandLine|contains: 'preinstall'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate npm packages that use preinstall scripts for setup.
indicators.description: Detects the execution of npm `preinstall` hooks, a TTP used by the ChainDrop malware to activate its credential harvesting payload.
